intro: Two words can name the same thing and judge it differently. Many German words come in triples: a positive word, a neutral one and a negative one – sparsam (+) / – / geizig (−); preiswert (+) / billig (−, when it means shoddy); rüstig (+) / alt (0) / vergreist (−); wissbegierig (+) / neugierig (0) / indiskret, aufdringlich (−); Herausforderung (+ framing) / Problem (0) / Katastrophe (−); Duft (+) / Geruch (0) / Gestank (−); standhaft (+) / stur (−); mutig (+) / leichtsinnig (−); gründlich (+) / pedantisch (−); schlank (+) / dürr (−); bescheiden (+) / unterwürfig (−); Reform (+ framing) / Kürzung (−); entlassen (0) / freisetzen (euphemism). In each of the eighteen sentences the context forces one connotation; the cue says whether you need the positive, the negative or the euphemistic word, and every word that fits the context is accepted. This is how you read a press text’s stance from its word choice, and how you choose your own words deliberately in writing.
tips[0].title: Character: positive / neutral / negative
tips[0].text: sparsam / geizig, knauserig · selbstbewusst, souverän / arrogant, überheblich · standhaft, prinzipientreu / stur, verbohrt · mutig / leichtsinnig, tollkühn · gründlich / pedantisch, pingelig · bescheiden / unterwürfig, devot · wissbegierig / neugierig / indiskret, aufdringlich.
tips[0].trap: neugierig is neutral – it can be warm (neugierig auf die Welt) or mildly critical depending on context. When you need an unambiguously negative word, use indiskret or aufdringlich; for the positive, wissbegierig.
tips[0].check.why: stur and verbohrt are the negative words for sticking to your position; the fans need the positive one, standhaft.
tips[1].title: Age, body, smell: the neutral middle
tips[1].text: alt is neutral; rüstig (vigorous) and betagt (polite) lean positive, vergreist, überaltert and verknöchert are negative. schlank (+) / dünn (0) / dürr, ausgemergelt (−). Duft (+) / Geruch (0) / Gestank, Mief (−). Find the neutral word; the others show the speaker’s feeling.
tips[1].check.why: Geruch is the neutral middle; Duft is pleasant and Gestank is disgusting, so both show the speaker's feeling.
tips[2].title: Public language: framing, euphemism, dysphemism
tips[2].text: Herausforderung instead of Problem, Reform instead of Kürzung, freisetzen or Stellenabbau instead of entlassen: positive framing and euphemism. Randalierer or Chaoten instead of Demonstranten: dysphemism. A text that uses these words has taken a side without an opinion sentence.
tips[2].trap: billig is ambiguous: in an advert it can be neutral-positive (billig einkaufen), in a review it usually means cheap and shoddy. preiswert and günstig are safely positive.
tips[2].check.why: Reform frames the change as an improvement; Kürzung is the critics' word and Zerschlagung is openly hostile.
tips[3].title: Same thing, three temperatures
tips[3].text: Before choosing a word, place it on the scale: warm (+) – neutral (0) – cold (−). In analysis, list the loaded words of a text: their sign is the author’s stance.
tips[3].check.why: schlank is the flattering word, dünn the neutral one, and dürr says the person is too thin.
remember[0]: Find the neutral middle (alt, neugierig, Problem, Geruch); the words around it carry the judgement.
remember[1]: Loaded words reveal stance: Reform / Kürzung, Demonstranten / Randalierer, entlassen / freisetzen.
mistakes[0].why: billig can imply poor quality; preiswert and günstig are safely positive.
mistakes[1].why: geizig is negative; sparsam is the positive word.
mistakes[2].why: vergreist is pejorative; rüstig praises an old person’s vigour.
table.caption: Connotation scales
hook: Read a writer's stance from single words like Reform versus Kürzung, and choose warm, neutral or cold words on purpose yourself.
